label: <DEL> step in sequences containing several of p/s/f/b
explanation: 97% of activation mass is on the delimiter step (t == L, recall_idx 0); it is essentially silent on original-phase and copy-phase steps (the small original-phase activity is mostly at late original steps of long sequences). It fires on only ~12% of delimiter steps; which ones depends on the content of the original sequence, like a graded sum of token contributions. Long sequences fire more often (DEL-step rate roughly 2% at L=3 vs roughly 20% at L=9). The tokens p, s, f, b (and to a lesser degree j, a, z, 1) raise it, especially in early or middle positions; a first token of b, v or g also helps. Top examples are p/s-rich, e.g. b j p p s h y <DEL>. Requiring the DEL step plus at least two of p/s/f/b among the original tokens gives dev P 0.36, R 0.60, mass recall 0.72, and catches 83% of the top quartile. The rule is incomplete because the feature behaves like a continuous weighted sum, not a clean boolean condition.
